The unique-name rule is in and everything is recorded. Here's the **complete settled scope** for your bookmark app — 19 flows across saving, finding, organising, and managing. In plain terms:

**Saving & recognising**
- Save a link fast (one box, one click), with a quick editable review of the page's fetched title, description, preview image and icon.
- Duplicates send you to the existing entry to edit; a mistyped non-address is gently refused (and your text kept); a page whose details won't load can still be saved with your own title.
- Edit any field later — title, description, address, reading status, tags, notes.

**Finding**
- Live, case-insensitive search across title, description, address, tags and notes, with highlights and a full-collection count.
- Precise queries: "exact phrases", AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and `#tag` — operators work in any case; quotes force a literal.
- Save a search (text + included/excluded tags) under a unique name and reopen it anytime.

**Organising**
- A **To read** list you can mark read; a **Reference** view (everything not to-read).
- **Archive**/restore to hide without losing; permanent **Delete** with a clear, distinct confirmation.
- Freeform **tags** with tidy normalising and autocomplete from your existing tags; **Markdown notes** that render formatted, collapse when long, and stay searchable.

**Managing at scale**
- **Sort** by date added, recently updated, or title.
- **Bulk actions** on selected bookmarks (tag/untag, mark read/unread, archive, delete) with safeguards so you never touch hidden or whole-collection items by accident.
- **Offline copy** per bookmark (page snapshot or the PDF itself) and manual **Internet Archive** submission.
- **Import/export** standard browser-bookmarks files, keeping titles, tags and dates.
- **Display preferences**: default sort, items-per-page (display-only, with Show more), and text size.

**Scope boundaries**
- A private, single-person app reachable from your computer and phone; **no sign-in** this cycle.
- Deferred (recorded, not built now): visual polish, large-collection performance tuning, and possible future importing of live browser tabs.

The prototype at **http://maker:4001** demonstrates all of this behaviourally (with simulated page-fetching, offline capture and Archive submission, since a prototype can't reach live pages).

**May I now switch from exploring to building — implementing exactly this approved scope as the real application?** Once you approve, I'll move to Phase 2 (development); nothing gets built until you say go.
